atoms.text: The day of the competition finally arrived. Knut, his mother and his father all dressed in their nicest clothing—traditional troll costumes of lederhosen and tartan for the men and tartan dungarees for his mum. They stood by their bridge, chatting with friends and family who had come to support them. The bridge itself was beautiful. The sides were hung with wreaths of wildflowers, each stone glittered with polish and the river underneath shone clear and blue. Knut could see the hopeful shine in his mother’s eyes; she wanted to win the “most beautiful” category too.

The contest was conducted by the Spanning Society. The society consisted of around 40 members who were experts on all matters pertaining to bridges. On the day of the contest, pairs were sent randomly to each bridge in the city. For the first half of the day, the pairs would spend approximately 20 minutes at each bridge judging them in the categories “most beautiful” and “best balanced” before moving to the next bridge. After each bridge was judged by all pairs of judges, the final competition began. Under the watchful eye of the society, more weight would be gradually added to each bridge city-wide until the last bridge standing was declared victorious.

The second round was nearly complete. Their bridge had only one more set of judges to impress before the finals. The tension in the city was building. “Knut,” called his mother, “I want you to check under the bridge one more time. Look for anything that doesn’t look like it should and check on those birds! If they got more poo on the inside again, I don’t know what I’ll do!” Knut sighed heavily. He could not be more excited for the competition to be over. His mother was really going crazy. He had already checked under the bridge five times that day, and he highly doubted anything had changed in the last 30 minutes since he had been down there. He made eye contact with his father who raised his eyebrows and made shooing motions with his hands. He seemed to communicate sympathy with Knut while nevertheless choosing not to save him.

Knut made his way down again. He stepped into the water under the bridge and felt immediate relief on his big, hairy feet. What a warm day it was. He glanced around for a moment not really expecting to see anything new. But, for a second, he thought he saw something moving. Very curious. He stepped a little closer and noticed things that appeared to be tiny, almost translucent, little mites burrowing into the cement holding the bricks together! Now that he was closer, he could see they covered the bottom of the bridge. He could also see in the glow above the water many tiny particles of dust hitting the water from the bridge. They were destroying the glue holding their bridge together!

atoms.a: What were Knut and his family wearing?

b: ++He had already checked under the bridge five times.
He felt uncomfortable in his lederhosen.
His feet felt slimy in the water under the bridge.

atoms.a: What did Knut find under the bridge?
b: He found his neighbours spying on their bridge.
He found birds pooing on the bridge again.
++He found tiny, little mites eating the bridge glue.
